brief: Markets are pricing one theme at a time while the macro backdrop runs several at once. Softer core PCE, after BEA revisions cut July to 3.0% y/y with September printing at 3.0%, plus dovish Fed officials, repriced October hike odds from 70% to about 30%. BofA holds underlying inflation at 2.5% y/y, unchanged, and still expects the Fed to hike at both remaining meetings this year: a skip would be only the third early interruption of a hiking cycle in recent history, and Chair Warsh risks a credibility cost by pausing while core PCE sits near 3%. Cited upside risks are AI capex, up 90% y/y this year and 36% next, though with limited direct pass-through, plus energy costs and AI-linked wage pressure. Separately, reports of normalizing Middle East oil flows have not pulled Brent below $100. Each de-escalation resets the price floor higher via inventory depletion, and oil-price volatility itself, driven by the Iran war, is inflationary, raising escalation risk into the US midterms. BofA also argues rising global investment demand against insufficient savings is lifting r*, forcing the Fed to tighten just to hold financial conditions constant. Consumer spending stays strong even as sentiment weakens.
